climate.overview_html: Germany became the third major European economy after France and the Netherlands to adopt a national fossil-fuel phase-out roadmap, with cabinet approval on September 23 for a 2045 exit from coal, oil and gas — presented at UNGA on September 24 alongside net-zero plans from more than 60 other nations. The WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update for September–November 2026 places near-100% probability on El Niño persistence through end-2026 and identifies a developing positive Indian Ocean Dipole (~0.9°C) that will amplify El Niño’s regional rainfall deficits across southern Africa and Australia. Downstream atmospheric responses are now materialising: Super El Niño analog composites for October–December 2026 favour a strong Aleutian Low, a downstream ridge over the central and western US, and below-normal temperatures across the southern tier, consistent with the anomalously early September nor’easter now easing along the East Coast.

items.source: BNN Bloomberg / Oil Change International / energynews.pro
items.headline: Germany Cabinet Approves Fossil Fuel Phase-Out Roadmap September 23: 2045 Exit Target for Coal, Oil and Gas; Third Country After France and Netherlands; 65% Energy Still Fossil Fuels; Renewable Electricity 80% by 2030; EVs, Heat Pumps and Carbon Pricing as Primary Tools
items.summary: Germany's cabinet approved a national roadmap to phase out coal, oil and gas by 2045 on September 23, making it the third major European economy after France and the Netherlands to publish a formal transition plan. The strategy was presented at the UN General Assembly on September 24. The roadmap targets increasing renewable electricity's share of total generation from 55% to 80% by 2030, supported by accelerated electrification (EVs, heat pumps), strengthened carbon pricing under the EU ETS, and a coal phase-out by 2038. Critics note fossil fuels still supply approximately 65% of Germany's total energy. Energy-transition NGOs have called the 2045 target inequitable given Germany's historical emissions. No sector-specific interim targets were published alongside the cabinet document.

items.headline: WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update September–November 2026: Near-100% Probability El Niño Persists Through December 2026–February 2027; Positive Indian Ocean Dipole ~0.9°C; Equatorial Atlantic SSTs Above Normal; Southern Africa and Australia Rainfall Deficits Expected
items.summary: The WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update for September–November 2026, compiled from Global Producing Centres' multi-model ensemble forecasts, places near-100% probability on continued strong El Niño conditions through the SON season and into December 2026–February 2027. The seasonal average Niño 3.4 SST anomaly is forecast near +3.6°C during SON, consistent with a historically strong event. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole (~0.9°C seasonal mean) is forecast to develop concurrently, which will amplify reduced rainfall across southern Africa, Indonesia and Australia while supporting above-normal precipitation over East Africa. The equatorial Atlantic is forecast to remain above-normal, reducing tropical development in that basin but contributing to enhanced northward moisture transport over Central America and the Caribbean through November.

items.headline: Super El Niño October–December 2026 Regional Outlook (September 26): Strong Aleutian Low Signals Downstream US Ridge; Below-Normal Temperatures Southern/Western US; Above-Normal Precip Pacific Northwest and Great Lakes; Analog Composites Based on 1982–83, 1997–98 and 2015–16 Events
items.summary: Weather.com's Super El Niño seasonal outlook published September 26 applies analog composites from the 1982–83, 1997–98 and 2015–16 events to the current Niño 3.4 anomaly of approximately +3.6°C. The composites favour an amplified Aleutian Low driving a downstream ridge across central and western North America, a storm track displaced southward into California and the southern tier, below-normal temperatures across the southern US and anomalously active West Coast precipitation. The Pacific Northwest and Great Lakes regions face above-normal precipitation risk through November. The anomalously early and intense September nor'easter and the record western Pacific typhoon season are consistent with enhanced global atmospheric energy typical of strong El Niño autumns.

weather.overview_html: Two new major hazards dominate the September 28 global picture. In the Central Pacific, Hurricane Nolo rapidly intensified to Category 4 with 145 mph maximum sustained winds, making a close pass south-southwest of Hawaii; high wind warnings remain for the Big Island and Maui County and a hurricane watch covers the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument from Nihoa to French Frigate Shoals. On the US East Coast, an unusually powerful early-season nor’easter killed at least one person in New York City, knocked out power to more than 136,000 customers across five states and produced Atlantic City’s highest coastal flooding since Superstorm Sandy, with conditions easing through Monday September 28. In the western Pacific, Typhoon Queenie (Surigae) is approaching peak intensity near Okinawa at 955 hPa and 150 km/h sustained winds, and is forecast to track toward the Izu Islands and the Tōkai and Kantō regions of Japan by late Wednesday–Thursday before extratropical transition; the 2026 western Pacific season has now reached the highest September cyclone count since 1966 according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.

items.source: NHC / Weather.com / AccuWeather / Hawaii News Now
items.headline: Hurricane Nolo Central Pacific — Category 4 UPDATED September 27–28: 145 mph Maximum Sustained Winds; ~380 Miles SSW Honolulu; Hurricane Watch Papahanaumokuakea (Nihoa to French Frigate Shoals); High Wind Warnings Big Island and Maui; Gradual NW Turn Tonight; First Major Hurricane 2026 Central Pacific Season
items.summary: Hurricane Nolo rapidly intensified to Category 4 on September 27, with maximum sustained winds of 145 mph (125 kt) and a minimum central pressure near 950 hPa, becoming the first major hurricane of the 2026 Central Pacific hurricane season. At the September 28 advisory, the center was located approximately 380 miles south-southwest of Honolulu, tracking west-northwest at 12 mph. NHC forecasts a gradual turn toward the northwest overnight, with the storm passing well south and southwest of the main Hawaiian Islands. A hurricane watch is in effect for the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument from Nihoa west to French Frigate Shoals. High wind warnings remain for portions of the Big Island and Maui County with gusts to 75 mph possible. Rainfall totals over 14 inches were recorded at the highest Big Island elevations through September 27. The storm track keeps the most populated Hawaiian Islands from direct landfall impacts, but significant surf and localised wind damage are ongoing.

items.source: CBS News / NBC News / Fox Weather / Washington Post / Yahoo News Live
items.headline: September 2026 Nor’easter (September 26–28): Deadly Early-Season Storm Kills One in New York City; 136,000+ Power Outages NJ/NY/CT/MA/RI; Atlantic City Flooding Worst Since Superstorm Sandy; NJ Governor Declares State of Emergency for Eight Counties; Conditions Improving Monday
items.summary: An anomalously early and intense nor'easter struck the US East Coast from North Carolina's Outer Banks to southern Maine between September 26–28. A New York City Housing Authority employee died after a tree fell in East New York, Brooklyn, on September 27. Power outages peaked at approximately 136,000 customers across New Jersey, New York, Connecticut, Massachusetts and Rhode Island. Atlantic City recorded its highest coastal water levels since Superstorm Sandy in 2012, with the surge amplified by a coincident full moon. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill declared a state of emergency for eight counties. Wind gusts reached 60 mph in Boston and up to 5 inches of rain fell across coastal New England. The storm's anomalous September timing and slow movement reflect a mid-latitude blocking pattern consistent with the strong Aleutian Low amplification expected in Super El Niño autumns.

items.headline: Typhoon Queenie (Surigae / JTWC 25W) UPDATED September 28: Peak Intensity 131 km SSE Kadena Air Base Okinawa; 955 hPa / 150 km/h Sustained / Gusts 215 km/h; JTWC Super Typhoon Classification; Track toward Tōkai/Kantō by Late Wednesday–Thursday; Extratropical Transition to Follow; Season Record Highest September Tally Since 1966
items.summary: Typhoon Queenie (Surigae, JTWC 25W) is approaching peak intensity on September 28, positioned 131 km south-southeast of Kadena Air Base on Okinawa, with a minimum central pressure forecast at 955 hPa and maximum sustained winds of 150 km/h (gusts to 215 km/h). The JTWC has issued a super typhoon classification. The system is tracking east-northeastward and is forecast to pass south of Okinawa at peak intensity September 28–29 before accelerating toward the Izu Islands, with its closest approach to the Tōkai and Kantō regions of Japan expected late Wednesday–Thursday, October 1–2. Extratropical transition is forecast shortly thereafter. This represents a meaningful track adjustment northward from the September 27 guidance, raising the risk of significant wind and rainfall impacts for the Greater Tokyo Metropolitan Area. Gale warnings and storm surge advisories are in effect across the Nansei and Izu Islands. The Japan Meteorological Agency notes the 2026 western Pacific season has produced the highest September cyclone count since 1966.

renewables.overview_html: With no major new transactions closing in the September 25–28 window beyond the projects already indexed this week, the EIA’s September 2026 Short-Term Energy Outlook projects US solar generation at +21% in 2026 and +18% in 2027, with wind at +7%; combined wind and solar supplied 20% of US electricity in H1 2026 for the first time on a half-year basis. Total new US generating capacity additions are forecast at a record 86 GW in 2026, led by utility-scale solar, as data-centre and advanced-manufacturing electricity demand drives build-out. The near-peak approach of Typhoon Queenie to Okinawa raises short-term curtailment risk for offshore wind installations in the Izu and Kii Channels.

items.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration / Utility Dive
items.headline: EIA September 2026 Short-Term Energy Outlook: US Solar Generation +21% in 2026 (+18% in 2027); Wind +7% (+5% in 2027); Record 86 GW Total New Capacity Expected in 2026; Commercial Electricity Sales +3.3%; Combined Wind and Solar Reach 20% of US Generation
items.summary: The EIA September 2026 Short-Term Energy Outlook projects US solar generation will grow 21% in 2026 and 18% in 2027, with utility-scale solar remaining the dominant new capacity source. Wind generation is forecast to grow 7% in 2026 and 5% in 2027. Combined wind and solar contributed approximately 20% of US electricity generation in H1 2026, a milestone representing approximately 10% growth year-on-year. Total new US generating capacity additions are expected to reach a record 86 GW in 2026, driven by utility-scale solar and battery storage. The commercial sector is forecast to see electricity sales grow 3.3% in 2026, with advanced data-centre and manufacturing loads accounting for the majority of the increment. ERCOT is projected to add approximately 18 billion kWh of solar generation in 2026 and 20 billion kWh in 2027.

items.headline: US Wind and Solar H1 2026: Output Climbed 10% Year-on-Year to ~420 TWh; 20% of US Electricity Generation; Outpaced Both Coal and Nuclear Despite Federal Permitting Headwinds; Investors Spent Record First-Half 2026 Amount on Solar-Plus-Storage Projects
items.summary: US wind and solar generation climbed approximately 10% year-on-year in H1 2026, producing nearly 420 terawatt-hours and achieving a combined share of approximately 20% of total US electricity generation — surpassing both coal and nuclear sources on a half-year basis for the first time. The growth was driven by continued capacity additions despite federal permitting headwinds, with ERCOT and MISO leading new solar additions. Investors committed a record amount in H1 2026 to projects combining renewable energy — primarily solar — with battery storage, reflecting improving economics and data-centre offtake demand. The EIA September 2026 STEO confirms the H1 trend will accelerate through the remainder of 2026.

science.overview_html: Two arXiv papers not indexed in prior editions enter the digest this cycle. Neptune (arXiv:2609.08606) introduces a hybrid CNN+SFNO ocean emulator for global subseasonal-to-seasonal prediction at 0.25° resolution, demonstrating skillful 60-day forecasts of 3D ocean temperature, salinity, SSH and sea ice and successfully reproducing the ENSO and IOD climate indices — directly relevant to the current Super El Niño and positive IOD combination. A station-based evaluation of FourCastNet3, GraphCast and ECMWF HRES in Northern Norway (arXiv:2609.10564) finds that HRES retains a modest wind-speed RMSE advantage (2.89 vs. 2.96 m/s) and that all three systems substantially underestimate strong winds in complex-terrain fjords — extending the ERA5-inherited systematic bias theme identified at global scale by Landsberg & Barnes (GRL, September 24) into a high-impact regional context with direct implications for offshore wind energy yield estimation and storm-damage forecasting.

items.source: arXiv / Donno, Epicoco, Cafaro et al. / CMCC / Columbia University
items.headline: Neptune (arXiv:2609.08606): Hybrid CNN+SFNO AI Model for Global Ocean Subseasonal Prediction at 0.25° — 3D Temperature, Salinity, SSH and Sea Ice Through 60-Day Horizons; Two Variants Neptune-1 and Neptune-025; ENSO and IOD Climate Indices Verified; State-of-the-Art vs. ClimaX Ocean and FourCastNet Ocean Baselines
items.meta: Donno, Epicoco, Cafaro, Accarino, Amirian, Acquaviva, Nassisi, Iovino, Bracco, Masina, Gentine · arXiv:2609.08606 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 8 September 2026
items.summary: Neptune is an end-to-end data-driven framework for global ocean subseasonal-to-seasonal emulation operating at up to 60-day prediction horizons. The architecture combines Convolutional Neural Networks for local feature extraction and Spherical Fourier Neural Operators on a spherical geometry for global cross-scale interactions. The model is available in two variants — Neptune-1 (1°) and Neptune-025 (0.25°) — and is forced by prescribed daily atmospheric fields to emulate 3D ocean temperature and salinity at 24 depth levels, sea surface height, and sea ice concentration and thickness. Evaluated against RMSE, CRPS and ACC baselines across multiple ocean basins, Neptune achieves state-of-the-art skill versus ClimaX ocean and FourCastNet ocean baselines at 1–12-month lead times and successfully reproduces ENSO, Z20 and IOD climate indices. The unstructured-mesh capability and explicit sea-ice module make Neptune particularly relevant for polar ocean processes and marine-heatwave prediction in the current Super El Niño / positive IOD context.

items.headline: Station-Based Evaluation ML Weather Models Northern Norway (arXiv:2609.10564): FourCastNet3 RMSE 2.96 m/s, GraphCast 2.94 m/s vs. HRES 2.89 m/s Wind Speed; All Models Substantially Underestimate Strong Winds in Complex-Terrain Fjords; No Evidence of Post-Training Performance Degradation
items.summary: This paper benchmarks FourCastNet3 (FCN3) and GraphCast against ECMWF HRES for wind speed using multi-year station observations in Northern Norway, where narrow fjords and rapidly changing orography create highly variable local conditions that global model grids cannot resolve. HRES marginally outperforms both ML models overall (RMSE 2.89 m/s vs. 2.96 for FCN3 and 2.94 for GraphCast), but FCN3 performs best under high-wind conditions. The most operationally significant finding is that all three systems substantially underestimate extreme wind speeds in complex-terrain fjords — a systematic bias with direct consequences for wind energy yield estimation, storm-damage forecasting and maritime search-and-rescue in the Norwegian Arctic. The ML models show no clear performance degradation beyond their training periods. The result extends the ERA5-inherited intensity-underestimation theme identified by Landsberg and Barnes (GRL, September 24) into a regional, high-impact context, and suggests that complex-terrain station evaluations represent a critical gap in standard global ML-weather benchmarking.

items.title: European Commission Announces EU Climate Insurance Alliance September 16 — Insurers, Investors, Risk Modelers and Public Authorities to Close Europe’s Climate Protection Gap; Only 25% of EU Catastrophe Losses Currently Privately Insured; Von der Leyen State of the Union Address; Parametric and Group Insurance Named Priority Tools
items.body_html: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the formation of a “climate insurance alliance” on September 16 in her State of the Union address, noting that only one quarter of catastrophe losses across the EU are privately insured, with the majority falling on national budgets and uninsured households. The alliance will convene insurers, investors, risk modelers and public authorities to increase coverage uptake and promote risk-reduction tools including parametric and group insurance; it was triggered directly by the 2026 European wildfire season and successive heatwaves, with France Assureurs citing approximately €500 million in insured wildfire losses from France alone. The announcement mirrors the mechanism underpinning the EU’s InsuResilience partnership and positions Brussels to legislate minimum catastrophe insurance requirements for mortgage holders and SMEs if voluntary uptake targets are not met by 2028.

items.title: Artemis Week Ending September 27: Enstar Fronts for ILS Capital Managers; Property Aggregate Excess-of-Loss Capacity +50%; Verisk Data: Q2 2026 Among Most Costly Quarters on Average Property Claims Cost; Demand Rising for Blended Liquid Cat Bond + Private ILS Portfolios Amid Live Event Risk from Queenie and Nolo
items.body_html: The Artemis bulletin for the week ending September 27 leads with Enstar beginning to front for third-party capital providers including ILS managers — a diversifying solution that expands the footprint of collateralised reinsurance into specialty lines where ILS structures have historically underperformed. Additional highlights include a 50% increase in traded property aggregate excess-of-loss limits, reflecting renewed appetite for aggregate covers after several years of post-climate-loss capacity contraction. Verisk’s latest average property claims cost data indicate Q2 2026 is on track to rank among the most expensive quarters on record; demand for blended liquid cat bond and private ILS portfolio products is rising as allocators seek liquidity in a week when live event risk from Typhoon Queenie near Okinawa and Hurricane Nolo near Hawaii simultaneously elevate ILS mark-to-market exposure.
